definition: Continuous passive motion uses a motorized device to move a joint repeatedly through a prescribed range without active muscular effort from the patient.
example: A clinician checks that a prescribed device moves the patient’s joint within the authorized range.

definition: Contour plowing follows lines of similar elevation across a slope to reduce runoff and soil erosion.
example: A grower aligns field passes with the hillside’s contours rather than straight down the slope.

definition: Contract review examines proposed or existing terms to identify obligations, ambiguities, risks, and deviations from intended arrangements.
example: A project team compares a service agreement’s acceptance criteria with its negotiated scope.

definition: ControlLogix is a Rockwell Automation platform for programmable industrial controllers and associated modules.
example: An automation engineer monitors whether an approved process sequence advances as specified.

definition: ControlUp provides software for monitoring and managing digital workspaces, endpoints, and virtual desktop environments.
example: An administrator checks whether slow desktop sessions share the same infrastructure bottleneck.

definition: Copier troubleshooting diagnoses copying equipment problems and checks whether corrective actions restore expected operation.
example: A technician distinguishes a paper-feed fault from a print-quality problem before replacing parts.

definition: A coping saw is a hand saw with a narrow replaceable blade stretched in a frame for cutting curves and intricate shapes.
example: A carpenter uses a coping saw to trim decorative molding to match an adjoining profile.

definition: Coppermine Photo Gallery is web software for publishing and managing albums, images, and related user interactions.
example: A site administrator organizes a community’s uploaded photographs into albums with appropriate permissions.

definition: Copywriting creates text intended to inform, persuade, or prompt a specific response from an audience.
example: A writer drafts a donation page that explains the cause and asks readers for a specific action.

definition: Core Spotlight is an Apple framework that lets applications index their content for search on the device.
example: A notes app makes a saved note discoverable from the device’s search interface.

definition: CoreOS refers to a container-focused Linux operating system lineage and associated tooling for running workloads on clustered infrastructure.
example: A maintainer reviews documentation for the specific CoreOS distribution in an archived cluster.
sense_note: Clarify whether the label denotes historical Container Linux, Fedora CoreOS, or another related project.

definition: Corona SDK was a Lua-based development kit for creating and deploying primarily two-dimensional apps and games across platforms.
example: A game developer writes a single Lua scene and runs it on several supported mobile devices.
sense_note: This is the app development toolkit associated with Solar2D, not a renderer with a similar name.

definition: Coronal polishing removes superficial stains and plaque from the exposed surfaces of teeth using dental polishing methods.
example: A qualified dental worker documents which accessible tooth surfaces were polished.

definition: Corporate communications manages official messaging and relationships with an organization’s internal and external audiences.
example: A communication team prepares consistent employee and press updates about a change in company leadership.

definition: The COSO Internal Control framework organizes the design and evaluation of organizational controls into complementary components and principles.
example: An internal auditor uses the framework to map how risk assessment and monitoring contribute to a reporting control.
sense_note: COSO also publishes an enterprise risk management framework; the label alone does not distinguish these.

definition: Cost estimating forecasts the resources and expenditures needed to complete a project or deliver an outcome.
example: A construction estimator combines material quantities with labor and equipment rates to develop a budget.

definition: Cost to serve estimates the expense of fulfilling and supporting demand for a given customer, product, or channel.
example: A distributor compares the fulfillment and support costs associated with bulk and small-volume customers.

definition: CoStar Real Estate Manager is software for administering lease and property portfolio records and associated financial or operational workflows.
example: A lease administrator checks renewal dates and reporting information for several sites.

definition: CPython is the reference implementation of the Python language, written primarily in C.
example: A package maintainer checks that a compiled extension works with the target CPython release.

definition: Crane signaling communicates authorized directions between a signal person and a crane operator using agreed visual or voice signals.
example: A lift team confirms its communication protocol during a supervised setup.

definition: Create React App is a toolkit for starting React projects with a preconfigured development and build environment.
example: A maintainer locates the build scripts in an existing project scaffolded with Create React App.

definition: CreateJS is a suite of JavaScript libraries for building interactive experiences with graphics, animation, sounds, and asset loading.
example: A developer uses CreateJS to animate objects in a browser-based illustration.

definition: Creative arts therapy uses structured engagement with artistic media as part of a therapeutic relationship and defined clinical goals.
example: A qualified art therapist incorporates drawing into a session designed around a client’s communication goals.

definition: Creative problem-solving reframes a problem and generates and tests alternative approaches beyond familiar responses.
example: A team develops several low-cost ways to reduce misplaced equipment and prototypes the most promising one.

definition: Credit risk analysis evaluates the likelihood and consequences of a borrower or counterparty failing to meet financial obligations.
example: An analyst studies cash flows and existing debt before assessing a borrower’s ability to repay.

definition: Creo Elements/Pro was PTC’s parametric mechanical design software lineage for creating parts, assemblies, and engineering drawings.
example: An engineer changes a controlling dimension and inspects the resulting assembly update.
sense_note: Do not conflate the historical Pro product name with Creo Elements/Direct.

definition: Crestron programming creates control logic and interfaces for Crestron room automation and audiovisual systems.
example: An integrator programs a room interface to route an approved video source to its display.

definition: Crestron provides hardware and software for controlling audiovisual equipment, room systems, and automation functions.
example: A meeting room uses a Crestron controller to coordinate its display, lighting, and audio.
sense_note: The label is a vendor and product family rather than one controller or programming language.

definition: Crime analysis examines incident and contextual data for patterns relevant to prevention, investigation, or resource planning.
example: An analyst checks whether reported theft patterns changed after a public reporting campaign.

definition: Crime mapping uses geographic information to explore the locations and spatial patterns of reported incidents.
example: An analyst maps incident counts by area and checks whether boundaries or reporting differences influence the pattern.

definition: Crime scene investigation documents a scene and identifies and preserves potential evidence for later examination.
example: An investigator records the location and handling history of collected evidence.

definition: The critical path method analyzes dependencies and duration estimates to identify the activity sequence that determines a project’s earliest completion.
example: A scheduler identifies which installation delay would move the overall completion date.

definition: Critical reflection examines experience, evidence, and assumptions to reconsider judgments and improve future action.
example: A student compares a group decision with what happened and explains which assumption they would revise.

definition: Critical test results management ensures that findings requiring urgent clinical attention are identified, communicated, and documented reliably.
example: A laboratory team confirms receipt of a critical result by the responsible clinician according to its protocol.

definition: Cross-platform app development builds applications intended to operate across multiple operating systems or device types, often sharing code or tooling.
example: A team tests a shared mobile application on iOS and Android while adapting platform-specific accessibility behavior.

definition: CryEngine is a game engine and authoring environment for building and running interactive three-dimensional applications.
example: A game team assembles terrain, lighting, and gameplay objects in a test level.

definition: CU-SeeMe was an early Internet videoconferencing application that transmitted live video between networked participants.
example: A digital archivist describes how an early remote classroom used CU-SeeMe to connect participants.

definition: Cucumber.js is the JavaScript implementation of Cucumber that runs behavior specifications against JavaScript step definitions.
example: A test checks that a scenario describing checkout invokes the JavaScript code needed to verify the workflow.

definition: Cucumber is a behavior-driven development tool that executes scenarios written in a structured natural-language format against step definitions.
example: A product team and developers use an executable scenario to verify what should happen after an invalid sign-in.
sense_note: The family includes multiple language implementations; Cucumber.js is one of them.

definition: Cultural sensitivity recognizes that cultural practices and assumptions differ and responds respectfully without treating individuals as stereotypes.
example: A facilitator asks participants how they prefer to be addressed instead of presuming a norm.
